title: The lattice bound $2d+1$
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and a field $k$ with $\operatorname{char}(k)>0$ and $\ell$ invertible in $k$. Let $X,Y$ be separated finite-type $k$-schemes and $p$ a $k$-morphism, as in [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Let $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be finite, with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\pi_E$. Retain the situation of [det-proper-heart-bound-torsion]: $p\colon X\to Y$ is proper, $d\in\mathbf Z$ bounds the dimensions of its geometric fibres, $V\to Y$ is an affine weakly contractible object of $Y_{\mathrm{proét}}$, $X_V=X\times_YV$, $a\colon S\hookrightarrow X$ is locally closed, and $L_0$ is a lisse finite free module over the pulled-back integral coefficient sheaf $\mathcal O_{E,S}$. The locally closed $k$-subscheme $S$ belongs to the same finite-type setting; no finite-type or Noetherian hypothesis is imposed on $V$ or $X_V$. Here $a_!$ is the locally closed extension by zero, and $H^q(X_V,a_!L_0)$ means pro-étale cohomology of the restriction of $a_!L_0$ to $X_V$. Then
$$
H^q(X_V,a_!L_0)=0\qquad(q>2d+1).
$$

external.place: *Sections.* $R\Gamma(X_V,-)$ preserves products (a product of K-injective complexes is K-injective, and sections preserve products) and cones, hence derived limits of sequences: $$ R\Gamma(X_V,a_!L_0)=R\varprojlim_nR\Gamma\bigl(X_V,a_!(L_0/\pi_E^n)\bigr). $$ *Milnor.* The Milnor sequence ([sk-prop-pe-milnor], or its version for abelian groups) $$ 0\to\varprojlim^1_nH^{q-1}\bigl(X_V,a_!(L_0/\pi_E^n

proof.text: On the finite-type source X, the locally closed extension of the lisse lattice is constant-model constructible: finite local models give a finite stratification, and quasi-compact open extension and closed pushforward preserve it. Apply the proved complete_sheaf helper of QcqsIntegralFiniteModelCompleteness. The strict completion augmentation is an isomorphism, and AdicCompletion.roos_isDerivedLimit identifies its target with the derived limit of the canonical integralLevel tower. Transport the Roos triangle back to K using this isomorphism. No completeness statement is applied to the possibly non-Noetherian base change.

source.place: Completeness, Sections and Milnor paragraphs; Lean realization using the cited existing declarations

proof.text: Forget the integral module action, then apply abelian-sheaf inverse image along r:X_V to X. Forgetting is exact and preserves products. The projection r is weakly etale, and its inverse image is isomorphic to localization restriction, which preserves products. Repleteness gives exact countable products for the internal modules and abelian sheaves. The generic countable-product properties show directly, using representatives and the localization Q, that both exact derived functors preserve products. Their degree-zero comparisons identify their image of each sheaf with its underlying abelian sheaf restricted to X_V.

proof.text: Derived global sections preserve products because they are right adjoint to the exact derived constant-sheaf functor, by mapDerivedCategoryRightDerivedAdjunction. They are triangulated. For the composite Phi of forgetting, inverse image and derived sections, apply Phi to the canonical Roos triangle. The product comparison intertwines the two transition endomorphisms, as verified after every product projection; transport the image distinguished triangle to get a Roos triangle for Phi(K).

proof.text: For d<0, invariance of fibre dimension under extension to an algebraic closure (topologicalKrullDim_pullback_eq_of_field) transfers the bound to the ordinary fibre over p(x). The point x supplies a point of this fibre; the closure of that point is a nonempty irreducible closed set, so the dimension is at least zero, contradicting the bottom bound. Thus X is empty. All sections of a sheaf on X are terminal, hence its underlying abelian sheaf is zero, and all the functors in the conclusion send it to zero.

source.place: Completeness, Sections and Milnor paragraphs; Lean realization using the cited existing declarations

proof.text: For d>=0, identify integralLevel K n with the scalar-cone reductionFunctor at exponent n+1. Both comparisons come from the principal reduction cone calculus and the two-term derived Nakayama resolution; their uniformizer endomorphisms agree sectionwise. The first conjunct of properHeartBoundTorsion identifies this reduction of K with the locally closed extension of the ordinary quotient of the lattice. Its second conjunct gives zero homology in every degree z>2d after Phi. Only individual level isomorphisms are used, so no compatibility of independently chosen comparisons is required.

proof.text: Homology of countable products in D(Ab) is the product of the homologies. For q>2d+1, the product vertices of the mapped Roos triangle therefore have zero homology in degrees q-1 and q. Exactness of the homology sequence of this triangle forces H^q(Phi(K)) to vanish. This is precisely the zero-outer-terms case of the Milnor argument, proved directly from the same triangle. Transfer the result through the degree-zero exact-functor comparisons to the displayed cohomology object.

split_report.summary: Restored the inherited separated finite-type scheme setting explicitly (the imported standalone statement suppressed the Noetherian scope used by its proof). Replaced the sketch by five steps: integral lattice completeness using its canonical derived-reduction tower; weakly étale slice restriction; an explicit image Roos triangle; derived sections on a ringed site; and the abelian-group Milnor sequence with the torsion bound. No new nodes. The preliminary ringed-space and product-preservation citation mismatches were corrected before delivery. The original conclusion and bound are retained. The second reader made explicit that the standing finite-type scope applies to X, Y and S, not to the pro-etale test scheme V or X_V, and replaced the truncated imported Milnor source entry by exact source labels. The resumed worker refreshed the torsion citation after its statement changed and proved the negative-dimension-bound case directly before invoking its nonnegative-bound version; no integer bound is discarded. Maintainer reader (FIX): step 5 now proves the identification of H^r(C_n) with the torsion-bound group: the inverse image along the site object X_V is the slice restriction (written out from the definition), and cohomology is independent of the coefficient ring (existing Stacks 03FD node); step 3's undefined t_n was renamed to the transition f_n. Maintainer reader (second pass, FIX): the inline proof that the pro-étale inverse image along the site object X_V is the slice restriction was moved into the new statement-only node lem-sfb-proetale-object-inverse-image-restriction (pro-étale analogue of lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-restriction); the long step 5 was divided into step 5 (d<0), step 6 (identification of H^r(C_n) with the torsion-bound group) and step 7 (Milnor sequence and conclusion); step 2 now cites the base-change functor of def-weil-proetale-inverse-image for X_V being an object of X_proét.
